results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * ol.quantity)) / NULLIF(SUM((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100, 2) AS overall_gross_profit_margin_pct FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% across the dataset from October 2025 to September 2026. This calculation compares your revenue (excluding GST) against your total product costs, using line-level pricing and discounts. Please note that any product variants missing cost data were automatically excluded from this calculation.
results.assumptions: Calculated across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Gross profit margin is (Revenue ex-GST - Total Cost) / Revenue ex-GST, using line-level prices, discounts, and ex-GST unit costs. Variants with NULL cost are excluded.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?

results.answer: Your top-performing product by gross profit for the year ending September 2026 was the One-Piece Swimsuit at $165,884.48 AUD, followed by the Shirt Dress at $130,441.22 AUD, Straw Hat at $108,854.01 AUD, High-Rise Jeans at $104,531.12 AUD, and Wool Coat at $89,912.11 AUD. This ranking excludes any product variants that were missing cost data.
results.assumptions: Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (treated as today). Gross profit is calculated as (line revenue ex-GST) minus (unit cost * quantity). Excluded variants with NULL cost.

    -- 17 days prior to June 19, 2026 is June 2 to June 18 inclusive (June 2 to June 19 exclusive)

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?

results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units between October 2025 and September 2026 were the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These totals combine all variants for each product and exclude any voided orders.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT round(avg(extract(epoch from (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o USING (order_id)
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation looks at the time between order and refund dates across the entire dataset. Please note that this is a general average and individual refund times may vary significantly.
results.assumptions: Calculated the average time difference in days between the order creation date and the refund creation date for all refund events across the entire dataset.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?

results.answer: Camel was your best-selling colour in winter 2026, with a total of 1,050 units sold. This excludes any voided orders and covers the period from June 1 to August 31, 2026.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN extract(isodow FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, round(sum(o.total), 2) AS total_revenue, count(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more total revenue than weekends, with weekdays generating 2,147,980.22 AUD across 11,153 orders compared to 1,173,950.49 AUD from 6,187 orders on weekends. This comparison covers all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, based on Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Comparing weekend (Saturday and Sunday) versus weekday (Monday to Friday) revenue across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) using order creation time converted to Australia/Sydney timezone. Revenue is gross order total for non-voided orders.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT p.product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS total_units_sold, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(l.quantity) DESC) as rn FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_type, p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title, total_units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY product_type;
results.answer: Your best-selling products by category are the One-Piece Swimsuit for swimwear (4,043 units), Straw Hat for accessories (3,619 units), and Linen Wrap Skirt for skirts (1,804 units). Other top sellers include the Shirt Dress (1,492), Ribbed Tank (1,395), High-Rise Jeans (1,295), Wool Coat (828), and Merino Crew Jumper (526). These totals are based on units sold across all non-voided orders.
results.assumptions: Calculated best-selling product within each product type by total units sold across all non-voided orders. Normalised product types using lower() where appropriate.
